questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Great city, with a lot of things to do. Nice weather and the fact that i could improve my Spanish during the exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fantastic experience, really glad that I went.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was an event for all the incoming exchange students, a few dates before classes started, where we were given all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Did not really need any assistance after my arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to be fair. I wrote a lot of people before i finally found a place to live. I would recommend using the sites Badi and Idealista. But you have to be patient as there is a lot of competition for housing, especially during the period, where new exchange students are moving to Barcelona.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to live in areas like Eixample, Gracía, Sant Antoni or Poble Sec. Those areas have everything you need, without being overly crowded. I would avoid living close to the campus, as it is far away from everything and there really is not much to do there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was done online, about a month before we arrived and everything went smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Honestly I did not need any help, but I think you could contact the Exchange Program Officer,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes that i wanted, so I was quite satisfied.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to get the classes you want, but do not worry too much, in my experience all of the classes. were quite interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Classes were for the most part interesting, and the way it was taught were very different than what I was used to. There were a lot of emphasis on student participation and often more discussion during class, than we are used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general the level was a bit lower than UCPH, but some classes were a bit harder than the others. From my experience Legal Aspect of Real Estate Transactions were the most difficult one that I had.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focused on oral participation from the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chinese Law and Culture, Legal Aspect of Real Estate Transactions, Diplomatic and Consular Law and Practice, Negotiation Skills, Comparative Constitutional Law and Intellectual Property, Patents and Trademarks.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiation Skills was my favorite class, would definitely recommend this one. The teacher is really great and you get to do a lot of practical negotiation exercises, which were a lot of fun.

questions.answer: Public transportation was a lot cheaper than expected, only 40 euros for 3 months with T-joven(youth card). Otherwise everything was as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not really participate in any, so I do not know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the beach during the start of the exchange, try to go to the beaches on Costa Brava, go to football games at Barca or Espanyol, go to the museums that the city has to offer and enjoy the bars and nightlife.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a weekend trip to other cities in Spain or go to Morocco, which is quite close.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think for me it was quite easy, there was not any culture shock or anything like that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think it is quite hard, my only interactions with the local students were doing group work with them. But usually the exchange students and the local students are a bit divided, because they are often not in the same classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. Some might not like the way that spaniards are not punctual, when it comes to time, for me this was not a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything was more relaxed and at a slower pace, which is something I am going to miss. Culture in general more leaned back and less stressed. Also the schedule is pushed a bit, so that lunch is later than in Denmark, dinner is usually around 9 pm, as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, go out and experience what the city has to offer. Remember that you are on exchange and not on a vacation, so do not worry about doing something all the time, it is okay to relax. Be open towards social interactions and meeting new people, this will be the best part of the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really much, but I would probably recommend to learn a little bit of Spanish before or during your stay, I think that makes you feel a bit more a part of the culture.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends from different countries and getting to experience living in a new country and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not really have any great challenges worthy of mentioning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
